headline: Ipamorelin
punch: The cleanest of the ghrelin-receptor agonists.

headline: What it actually is
body: A selective agonist at **GHS-R1a**, the ghrelin receptor, on pituitary somatotrophs. It signals through **Gq and PLC**, which is an entirely separate pathway from GHRH's Gs and cAMP route. | That separation is why the two multiply rather than overlap. Ghrelin signalling is the third arm of GH control, alongside GHRH and somatostatin, and it was only recognised as a system after the receptor was cloned.
punch: The third arm. Not a GHRH substitute.

headline: It does not raise cortisol
body: This is what distinguishes it inside its own class. Ipamorelin is **the only GHRP-class agonist that does not drive cortisol or prolactin elevation**. | GHRP-2 and hexarelin both do, through direct pituitary corticotroph stimulation. For anything you are running over months, a GH secretagogue that leaves the adrenal axis alone is a materially different compound from one that does not.
punch: ==The only one in its class that leaves cortisol alone.==

headline: It desensitises slowest
body: The GHS receptor internalises with repeated agonism, and the compounds are not equal. The desensitisation ranking is **hexarelin > GHRP-2 > GHRP-6 ≈ ipamorelin**, with ipamorelin at the favourable end. | So within a class defined by fatiguing, this is the one that fatigues least. That is a real advantage and it is why it is the default choice for longer use.
punch: Slowest to fade in a class defined by fading.

headline: It still fades
body: Slowest is not immune. GHS-R1a desensitises and internalises with repeated agonism across the whole class, and **24 hours of continuous GHRP infusion attenuated the bolus response** while 14 days of GHRH did not. | The human shape of this is the GHRP-2 data: more than 3-fold on day 1 falling to more than 1.8-fold by day 14 and 30. Expect the same direction here, more gently.
punch: Judge it at week four, not week one.

headline: Receptor occupancy decides
body: The pituitary responds to instantaneous receptor occupancy from the dose in front of it, not to your integrated daily total. At saturating doses you are paying for receptors that are already full. | Which means a single large bolus wastes a substantial fraction of itself above saturation, while the same total split across separate pulses produces near-maximal amplitude on each one.
punch: The pituitary cannot bank a dose.

headline: Space the pulses
body: Receptor availability recovers with time, and the recovery curve is the lever. At roughly 2 hours after a saturating dose, availability is around half of baseline but a fresh dose still produces most of a full pulse because the agonist saturates whatever has recycled. | At 3 hours availability is higher again. So spacing matters more than size, and the compendium's own conclusion across all this material was that fewer, well-spaced, well-anchored pulses outperform more frequent dosing.
punch: Fewer, wider-spaced pulses beat more frequent ones.

headline: Mind the gate
body: GHRP efficacy **is gated by somatostatin tone, not independent of it**, and is blunted by glucose, free fatty acids, glucocorticoids and exogenous GH. | So a pulse that lands after a carbohydrate load, or in the hours after exogenous GH, is landing into a closed gate. Placement against the somatostatin rhythm is worth more than adjusting the dose.
punch: A pulse into a closed gate is a wasted pulse.

headline: Bounded by physiology
body: Secretagogues raise endogenous pulsatile GH within a roughly physiological envelope. They **do not exceed exogenous GH's effect on linear growth** and they **cannot reopen a fused growth plate**. | And in rats, ipamorelin raised bone mineral content and cross-sectional area while **volumetric density was unchanged**. The bones got bigger rather than denser, which is what a growth-plate-mediated effect looks like.
punch: It works through your own axis, and inherits its ceiling.

headline: Verdict
body: The best-behaved compound in its class: selective, no cortisol or prolactin liability, slowest desensitisation, and a real synergy with the GHRH arm for mechanistic reasons rather than marketing ones. | Its limits are the class limits. It fades, it is gated by somatostatin, it cannot exceed what your own pituitary can release, and no trial has tested it against a height endpoint.
punch: Cleanest in its class. Still inside your own ceiling.
